Deep learning for lung nodule detection on CT: a randomized trial
Doe J, Roe R. Journal A. 2025. https://doi.org/10.1000/aaa

Abstract
We evaluated an artificial intelligence system for lung nodule detection on computed tomography.
The system improved sensitivity without increasing the false positive rate.

1. Introduction
Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer death worldwide.

2. Methods
This was a randomized controlled trial conducted at two academic hospitals.
We enrolled 240 adult participants referred for chest CT screening.
Participants with prior thoracic surgery were excluded.
The intervention arm used AI-assisted reading; the control arm used standard double reading.
Statistical analysis used mixed-effects logistic regression.

3. Results
Sensitivity increased from 81% to 93% in the intervention arm (p < 0.001).
Specificity did not differ between arms.

4. Discussion
AI assistance improved nodule detection in this setting.

Limitations
The trial was limited to two centers and a single CT vendor.

5. Conclusions
AI-assisted reading improves lung nodule detection sensitivity on CT.
